explain: G before a front vowel sounds like j.

fun.sv: Katten tycker att vi är gäster i hans lägenhet.
fun.en: The cat thinks we are guests in his flat.

explain: G before ö, a soft vowel, sounds like j: göra sounds like “jöra”.

fun.sv: – Vad ska vi göra idag? – Ingenting. Det gör vi bäst.
fun.en: “What shall we do today?” “Nothing. That’s what we do best.”

explain: G before a hard vowel (a, o, u, å) stays hard.

fun.sv: På vår gata finns det mer snö än bilar.
fun.en: On our street there is more snow than cars.

explain: U is a hard vowel, so the g in gul stays hard.

fun.sv: I november är solen inte gul. Den är borta.
fun.en: In November the sun isn’t yellow. It’s gone.

explain: K before a front vowel (e, i, y, ä, ö) sounds like tj.

fun.sv: – Jag ska bara köpa en lampa på IKEA. – Det sa du förra gången också.
fun.en: “I’m just going to buy a lamp at IKEA.” “You said that last time too.”

ask: How does the first k sound?
explain: The first k comes before y, a soft vowel, so it sounds like tj; the second k comes before a and stays hard.

fun.sv: – Det är tyst som i en kyrka här. – Nej, det är bara en finsk buss.
fun.en: “It’s as quiet as a church in here.” “No, it’s just a Finnish bus.”

explain: K before a hard vowel (a, o, u, å) stays hard.

fun.sv: Vår katt har inget jobb, men han är alltid trött.
fun.en: Our cat has no job, but he is always tired.

explain: Sk before a front vowel (e, i, y, ä, ö) sounds like sh.

fun.sv: – Hur mycket socker vill du ha? – En sked. Eller fem.
fun.en: “How much sugar would you like?” “One spoonful. Or five.”

explain: Sk before a hard vowel (a, o, u, å) stays sk.

fun.sv: Min katt går inte i skolan, men han vet allt om kylskåpet.
fun.en: My cat doesn’t go to school, but he knows everything about the fridge.

explain: Skj always sounds like sh, whatever vowel comes after.

fun.sv: Jag hade en vit skjorta. Sedan åt jag tomatsoppa.
fun.en: I had a white shirt. Then I ate tomato soup.

explain: Sj always sounds like sh.

fun.sv: Klockan är sju. Katten är vaken, så jag är också vaken.
fun.en: It’s seven o’clock. The cat is awake, so I’m awake too.

ask: Which word starts with the same sound?
explain: Tj always sounds like tj, and so does k before ö: tjugo and kök start with the same sound.

fun.sv: Det är minus tjugo grader. Finländarna säger: ”Lite kallt idag.”
fun.en: It’s minus twenty degrees. The Finns say: “A bit cold today.”

explain: In hj at the start of a word the h is silent, so hjälp starts with a j sound.

fun.sv: – Hjälp! Det finns en mygga i sovrummet! – Bara en? Grattis!
fun.en: “Help! There’s a mosquito in the bedroom!” “Only one? Congratulations!”

explain: In dj at the start of a word the d is silent, so djur starts with a j sound.

fun.sv: – Vilket djur är du? – En björn. Jag sover hela vintern.
fun.en: “Which animal are you?” “A bear. I sleep all winter.”

explain: In lj at the start of a word the l is silent, so ljus starts with a j sound.

fun.sv: I december tänder vi ljus, för solen har semester.
fun.en: In December we light candles, because the sun is on holiday.

explain: R + s blends into one sh sound.

fun.sv: Jag går en kurs i svenska. Min katt går en kurs i att sova.
fun.en: I’m taking a course in Swedish. My cat is taking a course in sleeping.

ask: Is the vowel long or short?
explain: One consonant after the vowel makes it long: tak has a long a.

fun.sv: Katten sitter på taket och tittar ner på oss. Som vanligt.
fun.en: The cat is sitting on the roof, looking down on us. As usual.

ask: Is the vowel long or short?
explain: A double consonant after the vowel makes it short: tack has a short a.

fun.sv: Mitt första ord på svenska var ”tack”. Mitt andra var ”kaffe”.
fun.en: My first word in Swedish was “tack”. My second was “kaffe”.

ask: Is the vowel long or short?
explain: Gg is a double consonant, so the ä in vägg is short.

fun.sv: Katten tittar på väggen i en timme. Vad ser han?
fun.en: The cat stares at the wall for an hour. What does he see?

explain: Kafé comes from French and is stressed on the last syllable, the é.

fun.sv: – Ska vi gå på kafé? – Ja, jag behöver kaffe. Mycket kaffe.
fun.en: “Shall we go to a café?” “Yes, I need coffee. Lots of coffee.”
fun.note: Kafé (café) is stressed at the end, kaffe (coffee) at the start.

explain: Most Swedish words, like kaffe, are stressed on the first syllable.

fun.sv: Finländarna dricker mest kaffe i världen. Jag hjälper till.
fun.en: Finns drink the most coffee in the world. I’m doing my part.

ask: How do you make the y sound?
explain: For y, round your lips as for u but say i.

fun.sv: Jag har en ny telefon. Katten har en ny låda. Katten är gladare.
fun.en: I have a new phone. The cat has a new box. The cat is happier.

ask: How do you make the ö sound?
explain: For ö, round your lips as for o but say e.

fun.sv: Min katt är söt. Det vet han, tyvärr.
fun.en: My cat is cute. Unfortunately, he knows it.

explain: Tak (roof) has a long a; tack (thank you) has a short a and a long k.

fun.sv: Det regnar in genom taket. Nu har vi en pool i köket.
fun.en: It’s raining in through the roof. Now we have a pool in the kitchen.

explain: Tack (thank you) has a short a and a long k; tak (roof) has a long a.

fun.sv: – Tack! – Tack själv! – Nej, tack själv!
fun.en: “Thanks!” “Thank YOU!” “No, thank YOU!”
fun.note: Tack själv is how Swedes say ‘thank you too’.

explain: Väg (road) has a long ä; vägg (wall) has a short ä and a long g.

fun.sv: GPS:en säger att vägen går rakt in i sjön.
fun.en: The GPS says the road goes straight into the lake.

explain: Vägg (wall) has a short ä and a long g; väg (road) has a long ä.

fun.sv: Jag tog fel väg och gick rakt in i en vägg.
fun.en: I took the wrong way and walked straight into a wall.
fun.note: Väg (road, way) has a long ä; vägg (wall) has a short ä.

explain: Glass (ice cream) has a short a and a long s; glas (glass) has a long a.

fun.sv: – Vill du ha ett glas? – Nej tack, jag vill ha en glass.
fun.en: “Would you like a glass?” “No thanks, I’d like an ice cream.”
fun.note: Glas (a glass) has a long a; glass (ice cream) has a short a.

explain: Ful (ugly) has a long u; full (full) has a short u and a long l.

fun.sv: Min väska är ful, men den är alltid full.
fun.en: My bag is ugly, but it’s always full.
fun.note: Ful (ugly) has a long u; full (full) has a short u.

explain: Kafé (café) is stressed on the last syllable; kaffe (coffee) on the first.

fun.sv: – Var jobbar du? – På ett kafé. Men de vet inte att jag jobbar där.
fun.en: “Where do you work?” “At a café. But they don’t know I work there.”

explain: Kaffe (coffee) is stressed on the first syllable; kafé (café) on the last.

fun.sv: Läkaren sa: ”Mindre kaffe!” Så jag köpte en mindre kopp.
fun.en: The doctor said: “Less coffee!” So I bought a smaller cup.

explain: Båt has a long å, written with a ring.

fun.sv: Vi har en båt men ingen sommar.
fun.en: We have a boat but no summer.

explain: K before ö sounds like tj, but it is still written k: kök.

fun.sv: Det bästa rummet på en fest är alltid köket.
fun.en: The best room at a party is always the kitchen.

explain: Hjälp starts with a j sound, but it is written with a silent h.

fun.sv: – Behöver du hjälp med svenskan? – Ja. Med alla ord.
fun.en: “Do you need help with your Swedish?” “Yes. With all the words.”

explain: The sh sound at the start of sjuk is written sj.

fun.sv: Jag är alltid lite sjuk på måndagar. Konstigt.
fun.en: I’m always a bit ill on Mondays. Strange.

explain: The tj sound at the start of tjugo is written tj.

fun.sv: Jag har tjugo par strumpor, men bara en strumpa i varje par.
fun.en: I have twenty pairs of socks, but only one sock in each pair.

explain: G before ä sounds like j, but it is written g: gärna.

fun.sv: – Vill du ha mer kaffe? – Gärna. Det är alltid svaret.
fun.en: “More coffee?” “Gladly. That’s always the answer.”

explain: Dörr has a short ö, so the r is doubled.

fun.sv: Katten vill ut. Jag öppnar dörren. Nu vill katten in.
fun.en: The cat wants out. I open the door. Now the cat wants in.

explain: Vägg has a short ä, so the g is doubled.

fun.sv: Väggarna är tunna. Jag vet vad grannen äter till middag.
fun.en: The walls are thin. I know what the neighbour has for dinner.

explain: Glass (ice cream) has a short a, so the s is doubled.

fun.sv: Glass smakar bäst i januari. Då smälter den inte.
fun.en: Ice cream tastes best in January. It doesn’t melt then.

explain: The sh sound at the start of skjorta is written skj.

fun.sv: – Är det en ny skjorta? – Nej, den är bara ren.
fun.en: “Is that a new shirt?” “No, it’s just clean.”
